extracted.intended_audience: Readers and prospective contributors to The Spectator; general literate public interested in manners, conversation, and periodical essays
extracted.subtask_short: writing periodical essays for general readers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing Spectator-style periodical essays and correspondence: humane, instructive pieces on manners, practical affairs, and social conduct that avoid scandal and appeal to a broad reading public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify gossip before repeating
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports advanced without a Person who can say whence he had it, or which is attested by one who forgot who told him it, or who had it from one of so little Consideration that he did not then think it worth his Notice, all such Testimonies ... are too slight to have any Credit against the Innocence and Honour of your Fellow-Citizen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not spread scandal or unverified reports; when an ill report is traced it often vanishes. Example: Cicero's admonition and the Lady Bluemantle anecdote—groundless stories commonly die away when source is examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid taking pleasure in speaking ill
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who are most pleas'd with the little Tales which pass about the Town to the Disadvantage of the rest of the World are culpable; the unwillingness to receive good Tidings is a Quality as inseparable from a Scandal-Bearer as the Readiness to divulge bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and writers should resist malicious delight in scandal; cultivate a temper that prefers truth and charity over slander.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widen subject-matter beyond learned wit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Paper should not turn altogether upon Topicks of Learning and Morality ... Things which are useful only to amuse Men of Literature and superior Education. It will consist also of all Things which may be necessary or useful to any Part of Society, and the mechanick Arts should have their Place as well as the Liberal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include content useful to non-literary readers (tradespeople, artisans, merchants) as well as the educated; diversify to serve a greater number of people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite authenticated contributions from all ranks
rubrics_metrics.description: I invite all Persons of all Orders, and each Sex, that if they are pleased to send me Discourses, with their Names and Places of Abode ... such their Labours shall be faithfully inserted in this Paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require names/places to ensure authenticity; publish pieces from a wide social range, from inventors to humble craftsmen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical case-histories of trades and shops
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be of great Use if we had an exact History of the Successes of every great Shop within the City-Walls, what Tracts of Land have been purchased by a constant Attendance within a Walk of thirty Foot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish detailed, practical histories and examples from trades and businesses to instruct and spur industry; concrete case studies are valuable for readers seeking practical advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include accounts of domestic virtue and female industry
rubrics_metrics.description: The Industry of the Female World is not to be unobserved: She to whose Houshold Virtues it is owing, that Men do Honour to her Husband, should be recorded with Veneration; she who had wasted his Labours, with Infamy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and honour household management, domestic virtues, and women's practical contributions as worthy subjects of periodical attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use narrative examples to teach practical consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: To awaken Caution and Attendance to the main Point, it would not be amiss to give now and then a Touch of Tragedy, and describe the most dreadful of all human Conditions, the Case of Bankruptcy; how Plenty, Credit, Chearfulness ... are in an Instant turned into Penury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative stories (e.g., bankruptcy) make abstract lessons vivid—use tragedy or case narratives to teach prudence in business and life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid terms of art and jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: It is necessary to caution [contributors] only against using Terms of Art, and describing Things that are familiar to them in Words unknown to their Readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write for the general reader: avoid specialized vocabulary or explain it; ensure clarity when contributors describe technical matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make content useful to practical pursuits (finance, husbandry, thrift)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ways of Gain, Husbandry, and Thrift, will serve a greater Number of People, than Discourses upon what was well said or done by such a Philosopher, Heroe, General, or Poet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise articles that teach readers how to prosper practically (e.g., stock histories, market behaviour, prudent buying) rather than purely rhetorical or scholarly pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be inclusive of minor inventions and everyday improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: If Things of high Moment meet with Renown, those of little Consideration, since of any Consideration, are not to be despised ... he who has found a Means to let the Instrument which is to make your Visage less horrible, and your Person more smug, easie in the Operation, is worthy of some kind of good Reception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise and publicize modest practical inventions and improvements alongside grand discoveries—they serve public interest and human convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage social moderation in conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is an impertinent and unreasonable Fault in Conversation, for one Man to take up all the Discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote conversational habits that give others room to speak; in essays and social commentary, model moderation and inclusiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid whining and excessive complaint in company
rubrics_metrics.description: The Valetudinarian ... has contracted an Habit of Complaint that he is sick ... That this Custom of his makes him ... fit only for the Infirmary ... There is nothing more improper than such a Complaint in good Company, in that they must pity, whether they think the Lamenter ill or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage characters or correspondents who monopolize sympathy through chronic complaint; cultivate self-awareness and restraint in social writing and depictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain decorum and modesty in public company
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a very great Indecency ... the strange Freedoms some ill-bred married People take in Company: The unseasonable Fondness of some Husbands, and the ill-timed Tenderness of some Wives ... I intreat Mr. SPECTATOR to correct such Misdemeanors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate modest speech and behaviour in public settings; critiques of indecency may be a valid subject for essays on manners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set generous, diverse role-models for youth
rubrics_metrics.description: It is highly proper to instill such a Reverence of the governing Persons, and Concern for the Honour of the Place, as may spur the growing Members to worthy Pursuits ... to set before the Eyes of Youth such Persons as have made a noble Progress in Fraternities less talk'd of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructive writing should present a variety of admirable examples (not just the locally celebrated few) to prevent vanity and to broaden ambition among young readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combat prejudice and sweeping generalisations
rubrics_metrics.description: General Charges against Bodies of Men is the Fault I am writing against ... it is to our Shame, that our common People ... have an irrational Contempt for the Language, Dress, Customs, and even the Shape and Minds of other Nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote impartiality, compassion, and recognition of differing talents; avoid and rebut broad, demeaning stereotypes in essays and correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure civility and basic etiquette in public spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: It is carefully provided that there may not be disagreeable Familiarities. No one is to appear in the publick Rooms undressed, or enter abruptly into each other's Apartment without intimation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commentary on manners should recommend concrete rules of decorum (dress, entry, restraint) and sanction breaches appropriately (anecdote: offender sent to Infirmary for throwing away cards).
